To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the monotonicity and the smoothness constraints are important for image segmentation, (b) we have developed efficient algorithms for the 2-D problem, and (c) we have proved that the 3-D problem is NP-hard.
(i) We present an O(IJK log K) time algorithm for the 3-D problem, where the size is I × J × K. (ii) We prove that the 3-D generalized version of the problem is strongly NP-hard.
we have presented a fast algorithm for segmenting monotone objects in 2D images and that a generalized version for segmenting monotonic objects in 3D images is NP-hard.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new class of image segmentation problems and provides the first polynomial time algorithm for the 2-D problem.
the development of efficient algorithms for the problem of image segmentation under monotonicity and/or smoothness constraints.
the problem of segmentations of monotone and smooth 2-D and smooth 3-D objects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the problem of segmentating monotone and smooth curves in 2-D is solvable in polynomial time and the problem of segmentting monotone and smooth surfaces in 3-D is NP-hard.
the monotonicity constraint is a useful constraint in the segmentation problem, and the proposed algorithm is an efficient solution for the problem.
the monotonicity constraint makes the 2-D problem tractable while the smoothness constraint makes the 3-D problem hard.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed efficient algorithms for the 2-D and intractable algorithms for the 3-D cases of the image segmentation problem.
we provide a fast optimal solution for a 2-D problem, and prove that a 3-D version of the problem is hard.

the monotonicity and the smoothness constraints are complementary in the sense that the 2-D problem can be efficiently solved by imposing one of these constraints and the 3-D problem can be solved by imposing the other constraint.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can solve a monotonicity and a smoothness constrained image segmentation problem in O(J2M) time, where M is the smooth parameter with 1 < M ≤ J.
monotonicity and/or smoothness constraints can be used to significantly improve the running time of image segmentation algorithms.
monotonicity and/or smoothness can help reduce the computational complexity of the image segmentation problem.
